title: Cozy Apple & Pear Crisp with Golden Oat Crunch
description: Make this easy apple crisp in under 30 minutes! Sweet apples, juicy pears, and a buttery oat topping create the ultimate cozy weeknight comfort food.
story: Rain was hammering against my kitchen window all afternoon, and honestly, my brain was completely fried from staring at emails. I needed comfort, and I needed it fast. I had a couple of Honeycrisp apples and slightly bruised Bartlett pears sitting in my Trader Joe's canvas bag. Instead of tackling a whole pie, I tossed together this easy apple crisp. The first time I tested this, I cranked my oven way too high and scorched the oats before the fruit even softened—lesson learned, keep it moderate! Filling my tiny apartment with the warm scent of cinnamon, melting Kerrygold butter, and bubbling fruit instantly reset my mood. Put on a good lo-fi playlist, grab a spoon right out of the drawer, and let's make dinner feel a little sweeter tonight.
ingredients: 4 large Honeycrisp apples, peeled, cored, and sliced into bite-sized chunks
2 ripe Bartlett pears, cored and chopped to match the apples
1/4 cup chopped pecans (optional, for extra crunch)
instructions: Step 1: Preheat your oven to 375 degrees F and lightly grease an 8x8 inch baking dish with a little butter or avocado oil.
Step 2: Toss the sliced apples and pears right in the baking dish with the lemon juice, 2 tablespoons of the brown sugar, and half of the cinnamon until evenly coated.

Step 3: In a medium mixing bowl, combine the rolled oats, flour, remaining brown sugar, remaining cinnamon, and chopped pecans. Pour in the melted Kerrygold butter and stir with a fork until moist, crumbly clumps form.
Step 4: Scatter the oat topping evenly over the fruit layer. Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until the fruit is bubbling at the edges and the oat crust is deeply golden brown.
proHack: Don't skip tossing the fruit with lemon juice! It cuts the sweetness and keeps the pears from turning brown while you mix up the oat topping.
storage: Cover any leftovers tightly with foil and store in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat individual portions in the microwave for 30 seconds or pop it back into a 350-degree oven for 10 minutes to bring that oat crunch back to life.

faqs.question: Can I substitute pears if I only have apples?
faqs.answer: Totally! Just use 6 total apples instead. Granny Smith or Gala work great if you want a different texture or sweetness level.

faqs.question: How do I prevent the oat topping from burning?
faqs.answer: If you notice the oats browning too quickly before the fruit is tender, loosely tent a piece of aluminum foil over the baking dish for the last 10 minutes.
